you can look past clunky visual presentation
you want to master complex rule sets

cohorts.summary: Players find the user interface instantly confusing and poorly designed.

claims.claim: The user interface is described as confusing, uninspired, and poorly designed.

citations.review_text:
Awful game
The graphics and artstyle are leagues better than Civ 6, but still overall worse than Civ 5 and much more cluttered.
Confusing UI
TERRIBLE character models and animation- somehow even more cartoony and overexaggerated than 6's.
Bizarre choices for leaders of civs.
Gameplay ranges from just ok to completely unfun. Combat is terrible, diplomacy doesn't work right, city management is bizarre. And WHY have they copied the changing civ gimmick from Humankind? This was one of the worst parts of that game, and they just brought it over wholesale, ruining the fundamental identity of what Civilization is.


Also, I am still permanently banned from their dedicated subforum, over a comment made on one of the dev diaries for one of the new leaders (YEARS ago, before game came out) where I agreed/responded positively to a joke another commenter made (in the lines of "Haha, very true"). The reason? "Banned for attempted to circumvent ban through making duplicate accounts". What. This is the only account I have ever had.........
If this is how they operate on their Steam forum, that should tell you everything.

I didn't play much, but what I played I just was so thoroughly unimpressed that I feel like I want to put my "don't recommend" review here anyway. The UI is honestly the most amateurish looking UI I've seen in a game of this scale maybe ever. The icons are honestly just horrible, the colourless and NOT colour coded approach to everything is both uninspiring and unclear, and the text, text boxes etc are all over the place. The characters and animations are a huge step back from VI, and while some of the map looks nicer than VI, it ends up a bland mess due to the previously mentioned issues. 

The age approach (even after updates) is limiting and removes the sandbox element of Civ, while also restricting the game to a very specific historical interpretation instead of us creating our own. Commanders are better, some details are better than in the past, but at the core the game just feels lifeless and dull compared to the earlier iterations. It feels even more just like you're just clicking on menus and tiles than before, and feels less like a "living" interactive thing somehow. Obviously, all of this is subjective and my review is based on a very, very short time in game, but it's saying something about the issues this game has at the most basic level that I feel like it's still worth adding this review regardless.

i did not play long at all, run out of time before the 'free week' ended. Still, not planning to purchase this game anymore. And I have played all of them, including the first one, thousands of hours combined. I just got so turned off immediately by the weird interface ideas. Simple example: each 'tooltip' comes with a giant 'inspect' button that seemingly does nothing at all. And a tiny 'close' button. Why? 

Another problem: in previous versions I was able to set in options to only display tips for advanced players. Not here. The moment you start you are absolutely overwhelmed with countless of tips on the most basic civ ideas.

The minimalistic interface is just frustrating. 

My biggest gripe with civ6 is how the game has evolved more and more towards a spreadsheet exercise and forces you to min-max all aspects of the game. Civ6 was also just too much work, too many mechanics. I always enjoyed the exploration phase, discovering the new land. I expected civ7 to reverse this trend but, again, in my very short playing experience, it has gotten worse. 

Very sad!

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the base game and its downloadable content are overpriced and feel like a cash grab.

citations.review_text: The game is compelling once you learn some of the new mechanics/strategies. I think the addition of leaders and civilizations with their own perks is great, but the starting amount is disappointing and the DLCs really feel like cash grabs on top of an already expensive game.  The DLC bundle didn't feel worth the thirty extra bucks I paid for it. The result is an old civ fan that's been around since the first game disillusioned with the direction of the franchise. Will think much harder before jumping into the next iteration if they continue this DLC squeezing blood from a stone trajectory.

The Worst Civ EVER (I've played the series since Civ 1)

(-) You have Napoleon x2 :D (I could say something here :D)
(-) AGES: Firaxis just killed the CORE of the series, which is playing as one civ without any resets until the atomic annihilation or robotic wipeout of the world.
(-) Crisis near the end of the age. It is a must no matter how great your civ is.
(-) Selection of Slavic countries
(-) Even the Space Age will be locked behind a PAID DLC ...
(-) Money grab: the base game + all DLCs have a horribly insane price.

(+) Nice graphics.
(+/-) They are trying to fix it (but anything that could make this game better is hidden behind an insane paywall).

If you like all prev games in the series, DO NOT BUY this one.

I’ll give this game a chance if the complete edition (with all paid DLCs) ever drops to $20.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering bugs and finding that game systems lack clear information or tutorials to explain mechanics like trade routes.

citations.review_text: I have never had such a frustrating time with a 4x game.  there is such poor information and explanations given to the player it is hard to understand where things like why my trade route won't work or where some negative is coming from.  encountered so many bugs and suboptimal design that it actually pissed my group off enough we just dropped our first run through of it completely.  I'd say the game is salvageable, but its been out for over a year and a half at this point...

I preordered this game, but personal issues meant I had to wait over a year after launch to play it. I should never have bothered.

Sid Meier’s Civilization VII has destroyed the series for me. I’ve loved Civ for as long as I can remember, but this game is horrendous.

The more recent editions of Civ added complexity, which I welcomed—even when it made the learning curve steep. Previous games offered clear descriptions and useful tutorials that helped you understand the mechanics. That is far from the case with Civ VII.

Buttons you’re directed to click for more information literally do nothing. The tutorials use a lot of words to explain very little of practical use. You can spend hours reading tooltips and still come away without understanding how things work.

Given the price of the game and its ridiculously overpriced DLC, I expected something enjoyable to play. Instead, I got an exercise in frustration.

Save your money. Beating your head against a brick wall would be a better time than playing this dreck.

I WILL NEVER SUPPORT THIS FRANCHISE OR FIRAXIS GAMES AGAIN!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as heavily automated, leaving players with little to do other than click through turn progression.

citations.review_text:
I should have listened to all the negative reviews. Luckily, I at least bought the game on sale.

As a long time CIV player with easily over 1,000 hours in each game of Civ 2, 3, 5, and 6, I wanted nothing more than to love Civilization 7. Instead, I am deeply disappointed, the game feels like an empty shell compared to the other versions.
The AI is completely unbalanced. Instead of playing smart, it just blatantly cheats/speeding ahead and pulling hundreds of science points out of nowhere with zero logical backing (yes i love playing on deity, so i don't mind they cheat a bit). But the game feels gutted, with far too much content locked behind day-one DLC and paywalls rather than being included in the base game.

I would love to play Civ 7, but in its current state, I just can't. The gameplay loops feel hollow. I am officially giving up on this one and returning to Civilization 6.

@Civ_Nuovis Thanks for responding! I really respect that you took the time to read my review and I appreciate your feedback. I am going to give the game a few more hours and complete a full match or two to see if it grows on me. For now, though, it feels a bit like an autoclicker experience where I just click 'next turn' while random pop-ups hand out gold or other resources.

I know we all see things differently, and looking back, I realize I wrote my initial review out of anger and disappointment. I want to expand on my thoughts more clearly.

I've played Civ II, III, V, and VI for roughly 600–1,000 hours each, plus another 500 hours in Beyond Earth. I’ve loved seeing how the series has evolved over the years, so my criticism isn't about being resistant to change.

To me, Civ VII feels like a step backward in player freedom. Removing builders, manual citizen management, traditional city-states, and barbarians, while also restricting city borders and simplifying overall empire management, has stripped away much of what made the s…

**Civilization VII – Where Did the “One More Turn” Feeling Go?**

When I was a schoolboy, I used to play Civilization III for hours. I remember staying up all night, completely absorbed in building my empire. There was always something to do, something to improve, something to plan. That famous "just one more turn" feeling was real.

After that, I didn't play Civilization for many years. Recently, I happened to discover that Civilization VII had been released, and I decided to give it a try. I was genuinely excited to return to the series.

Unfortunately, I'm disappointed.

I'm currently about halfway through the first Age. I have one city and three towns, I'm playing on a medium-sized map, and I've already explored my entire continent. I'm not at war with anyone, and I can't explore across the ocean yet.

And here's my biggest question: **What am I actually supposed to do?**

My city is constructing a building that takes 8–10 turns to complete. My towns require gold to develop, and I obviously can't afford to constantly buy buildings in all three of them.

Roads are built automatically. Tile improvements are largely automated. There are no workers to manage, no roads to plan, no farms or mines to build manually. My army has nothing to do because I'm not at war. My scouts have nowhere left to explore.

So what do I do? I just keep clicking "Next Turn." Again. And again. And again.

Yes, I understand that there are technologies to research, buildings to construct, diplomacy, trade, and long-term strategic goals. But these are occasional decisions. **What am I supposed to do during the 10 turns between them?**

In Civilization III, even when I wasn't fighting anyone, I always felt involved in developing my empire. I could manage workers, build infrastructure, improve land, develop multiple cities, and constantly make meaningful decisions.

In Civilization VII, it feels like the developers tried so hard to eliminate micromanagement that they accid…

citations.review_text: Absolutely scummy to have all these paid DLCs, and even scummier to have those DLCs not included in the "Settler's Edition" of the game, which I unfortunately paid for. What's worse is what you get with the DLCs, which is to say, not much: a couple extra leaders, a couple extra civilizations. Eh? They really hemmed-and-hawed about with this one, and while I want it to get better, I think regardless of whether it has a turnaround like Civ 6 did, there's really no denying that from launch up to this moment, the game is just a disappointment through and through.

So… this is one of the most difficult reviews I have ever had to give. I am enormous Civilization fan and I am extremely extremely easy to satisfy. I have played Paradox games and paid paradox prices and been happy as a clam. This games release and the last year or so of management has been extraordinarily disappointing. 

I was extremely hyped for this game. The leaders? Sick as hell. The civs, also cool. The art style, the narrator, the bold new vision, all seemed really interesting and cool! And then the game came out. The art style of the game itself was good but in a lot of other places it felt soulless, particularly the loading screens just were ghastly. The game felt so bare bones and half baked. You couldn’t even play “Just One More Turn”. It felt like a Civ game had been released for beta testing. 

Then the DLCs and expansion packs started coming out immediately and it left such a bad taste in my mouth. The expansions do not add nearly enough for the price they are asking for. If there were twice as many leaders and wonders and new mechanics or whatever, I’d be fine with it. Once again, I play paradox games, I’m no stranger to an expansion pack that costs too much money but at least (oftentimes) it’s worth it to get to add something new to the game. I cannot really say the same here. 

I am an extremely forgiving player and am more than willing to give the benefit of the doubt and take into consideration things like the cost of production, inflation, and whatever other factors have driven some of these decisions, but as of right now, I can’t recommend this game. The game is still not in a state that feels finished. It’s still lacking basic mechanics. Expansion packs don’t make up for it. The DLCs may be make it or break it for this game honestly and even then, the DLCS may not be able to wash out the bad taste in my mouth of a game being released half baked and then selling basic aspects of a game under the guise of add ons. 

I feel really bad leaving suc…

Not good, game gets boring after the antiquity age, and a lot of UI quality of life things in Civ 6 are gone. It's impossible to track city state Suzerain and Befriending status, unlike in Civ 6 where they had a page for it. If you're doing religion in the exploration age you have to identify religions by a tiny icon located on its name bar, and if you're looking at your general production of say gold, the page for that will list what each city is producing, but then they have "Other Sources" part and it's producing half my gold, which doesn't help me identify if it's through trade routes or policies. Plus everything in this game is poorly described, nothing tells you factory resources apply empire wide. It's a game where you have to play with google open just to make sure you're playing it right. Also they're selling civilization DLCs for the price of Gathering Storm, which is just ridiculous. Who is paying $30 for 6 civilizations you could just mod in. I will say I like the city/town system, and crises/events at the end of ages.

claims.claim: The game features an age system with transitions that interrupt gameplay and reset progress between eras.

citations.review_text:
There’s a lot I genuinely like about this version of Civ. City development with quarters adds great flavor by letting you place buildings directly on the map, and the city-and-town mechanic works surprisingly well once you get used to it—it makes complete sense that not every settlement is a sprawling metropolis. I also love that civilizations have distinct, customised visual looks for their units. For the most part, these new mechanics work well and still deliver that classic Civilization feel.

Where the game completely loses me is the Age system. Even with the adjustments made in Test of Time, it is outright abhorrent and completely jarring to gameplay. It feels like three different games crammed together like train carriages. I never played the release version before Test of Time, and I can't even imagine how much worse it must have been. You spend all this effort researching tech, expanding your cities, and conquering land—only for the game to come to a screeching halt and force a time jump. You lose that seamless, progressive march through history that defined previous iterations, replaced by a disjointed mechanic that just feels gross to play.

I have played 63 hours in the game so far and I also own the Civ 6 complete with DLCs and I must say this new game is totally different from the last one and I find the game mechanics much more complicated to understand and this new ages mechanic where you lose progress and kind of start over with some progress is a big pain. I like the new commander feature for troops but also a not so easy to use. The game has nice visuals but I feel it is a little complicated to understand compared to the last game and I feel you get a lot less in return for the investment as the game is very very expensive and I don't think I would buy add ons for this and spend the money as the base game hasn't captured my attention yet as something I want to play all the time. The learning of the game is hard and tiring. I don't like the spy mechanics in the new game either.  I don't agree with the settlement cap feature and also now only the first settlement is a city and after that your settlers create towns which you need to buy the upgrade to cities which is like Humankind. The new game are going this route of city cap and I don't  agree as the focus is for you to expand but they limit you to this feature as going over the city cap your happiness is penalised. Once playing the games and there are town upgrades to be done the game forces the screen to go the town for upgrades even if you don't have money to upgrade and the force screen thing is a pain to play the game as it has so many mechanics which is way to complicated if you just want to relax. Uprading your town eventually kind of gets capped and then you get specialisation which you lose with because it in many cases loses you happiness and costs money with only sometime giving you added science or culture. The buffs for this game in science and culture as not as good as in Civ 6 I think. The feature of ages now is very different and for example when changing ages you loose progress in a city state and your cities could go back to be…
A total mess, diplomacy, trade and religion, totally irrelevant. Just 3 eras when you change era everything resets and you start a new game this is frustrating.

claims.claim: The map and visual presentation suffer from clutter, making it difficult to easily locate units and structures.

citations.review_text:
I can't finish a full game nor feel enticed to want to play it regularly. I have been trying to figure out why that is and why I'm so drawn towards the games from the total war series. I think I've narrowed it down to two issues. 

My first issue is that the world/map is too graphically busy for me. I can't easily see and find things like my units easily. I think I'm straight up over stimulated. When I zoom out I want to get a lay for the land, but all I see is 'stuff' everywhere. I can't be bothered to use map filters- I use those when I'm in an analytics mood. I want to see my cities and my units easily and I'm visually impaired from doing so. I think this is why I spent ages playing and loving Civ 3. 

My second issue is that there are too many toil-based activities in the game for me. It honestly feels like my day job trying to figure out out where to place tiles and all the mechanics nowadays that go into it. To be honest, I don't really care for this level of detail in a Civ game. If I want that level of detail, I'd play Skylines.

I don't know. I just can't pretend I'm this benevolent ruler that crushes the insidious despots of the world. I'm too busy finding my units, assaulted by sprawling city graphics and busyness everywhere, and mired down in the muck and toil of tile placement and futile attempts to get them perfect.

The main issue I have with this is I don’t know what I’m doing and nothing is explained very well in-game. 

Once you get to the Exploration age, everything just becomes an informational mess. 

I never had this issue with Civ 6 or Civ 5 when I played them (albeit not a great deal either). 

They really need to clean it up if they want to expand into the Atomic/Information age as by the Modern era, the map is a horrible mess and a strain on the eyes. 

Also, the DLC is so half-baked. 

Bulgarians using Arab swordsman, Sengoku Japan using Mongolian archers, Carthage just looking the same as the Greeks. 

What drew me to Civ 7 before release was the asymmetry of the factions. They have given up on this now and just copy and paste half the assets from over Civs. 

I mean, Mongolian archers fighting for Sengoku Japan? Why can’t they just use the same model as Heian Japan anrchers? Also Samurai cavalry with shields. So much for historical flavour.

claims.claim: Age transitions break game momentum and reset progress.

citations.review_text: The graphics are genuinely excellent and some of the new systems are cool, but after 200 hours I still can’t get into it. Civ 7 takes too much control away from the player.A lot of the game feels overly autonomous. Towns mostly handle themselves, a bunch of decisions get forced on you through the age system, and things just… happen that you can’t really stop or meaningfully influence. The age transitions still break momentum even if you stick with one civ, and a lot of the mid-to-late game feels like you’re reacting to the game’s systems instead of actually playing the way you want.Civ 6 still feels far better. It gives you more meaningful choices, deeper systems to optimize, and actual control over your empire. I keep going back to it.There are good ideas here, and it looks great, but the lack of agency and the forced stuff kills it for me. Maybe it’ll get there in a couple years, but right now it’s not close.
Don't Like that I spent time making progress & lose it & have to start over is what it feels like at the end of the Age.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the in-game documentation and civilopedia as failing to properly explain core mechanics, such as the explorer unit and cultural victory systems.

citations.review_text:
Very disappointing entry in the series. My expectations for Civilization VII were high, and it did not come close to meeting them. The game feels flat, both visually and in how it plays.

The new mechanics have potential, but the in-game documentation does not support them. Key reports are missing, and the game rarely shows how its systems connect. The Explorer is a good example. The Civilopedia entry covers the history of explorers but gives no practical explanation of the unit: that it needs a Museum or University to research artifact sites, that research only reveals sites in that region, or how to open up additional dig sites later in the age. A player should not have to rely on outside guides to understand a core mechanic in a flagship 4X title.

What you could add

I don’t have your earlier Civ questions on hand, so these come from the Explorer problem and from gaps other experienced players commonly report. Use only the ones that match your own play.

Hidden unlocks. More dig sites open up through the Hegemony civic, but the game never makes that clear. Patch 1.1.0 changed it so that completing Hegemony grants an extra artifact each time an Explorer researches artifacts. A sentence like this works: “Critical progression unlocks are buried in the civic tree with no in-game pointer to them.” 
gonintendo
Tech and civic tree readability. A common complaint is that the tech tree makes it hard to tell what depends on what. 
steamcommunity
City building feedback. Reviewers note that the game shows very little about why a building has the adjacencies it does. 
nex-3
Comparison to earlier entries. A line such as “Civ V and VI set a standard for in-game documentation that VII falls well short of” gives your experience extra weight.
A closing verdict. For example: “Recommended only for players willing to learn the game from wikis and forums.”
They really phoned it in with this one. Poor UI, poorly explained mechanics, and the civlopedia is garbage

I have had this game since launch. I have played at least one game through each of their "we are fixing it" updates. But I am done waiting and it's time to call it what it is. 

There is no point in reviewing this game independently, CIV is a series and they are supposed to improve on the previous iteration. I have a thousand hours on CIV 6, so I understand the game and the format well. 

Here is why CIV7 sucks and is potentially the CIV killer:
- There is almost zero thought process put into any other victory type save Domination. Space race is no longer a race. Cultural victory is even more confusing than CIV6 with moving goal posts and a tourism system that is not explained anywhere. And the new economic victory is somehow more boring and pointless than the religious victory. There is no way to "compete" with AI in the economic victory. There is nothing you can do to stop an isolated CIV from magically becoming an economic super power and winning. (except war of course)
 
- Visual Design and UX teams were/are still working in complete isolation. While it looks pretty when closed up, there is no way look at a city and figure out what is going on. OR tell one city from another. Even wonders don't stand out. The only way to play this game is through menus and those look ugly. So all the efforts spent on making units and buildings look beautiful is completely wasted. 

- The resource assignment is the most Kafkaesque stupidity I have seen in any game. Why is it point and click? Twice? Haven't you heard of dragging? What about resource sorting by bonus type? Is all that to hard to implement? or just too hard to think about?

- Since war is the only system they truly improved on everything AI does boils down to war. There is no diplomatic way to prevent your neighbours from declaring war on you. No matter how much influence you spend on improving relations, they will at least declare 2 wars on you per age due to the idiotic agenda system. 

- The last stra…

Disappointing. The changes to gameplay are weird, the UI is buggy, the civlopedia doesn't explain things very well. It would be a kinda decent game if you didn't have to spend over $100 on DLCs to get the full game.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that military victory is significantly easier to achieve than other victory types, often overshadowing alternative win conditions.

citations.review_text:
Look, I've read so many comments and reviews, and a lot of them focus on how bad Civ 7 is compared to Civ 6. I don't think that's fair.

The Ages system is great, and the idea of switching civilizations is awesome. The variety makes the game much more interesting. After thousands of hours in Civ 6, Civ 5, Civ 4, and Civ 3, I think this is the first time I've actually tried playing every single civilization.

So what's my one real issue with this game? It's too easy.

The AI is still terrible at warfare and battles, just like in every previous Civ game. It can't concentrate its forces on your weakest points, and it keeps dragging out wars it has absolutely no chance of winning.

At this point, it's almost ridiculous not to pursue a military victory. It's so much fun to play militarily, and it's also the fastest way to turn your civilization into a genuine superpower. And yes, a cultural victory is still the easiest one to achieve.

Anyway, as a Deity player, I have to say that so far I haven't found a real challenge in this game. And that's a shame, because there's a lot here to love.

This game compared to its predecessors is atrocious. I gave it a fair shot, I really did, but I can't take this bull crap anymore. This is unacceptable. The main game and especially its DLC is grossly overpriced. 
The value to content ration in the DLC's barebone, NOT worth it! 

The gameplay loop is a sad disappointment, don't get me wrong there diffently are good improvements and some of the new mechanics are good. But the list for what is bad, broken or worse is longer. 
Inconsistent pathfinding, population (pop) management is feels just bad, 
especially because it is so reliant on policies to even be somewhat descent. Lack of support units, no commanders does not suffice, even they are awkward to use. The lack of identity now that Leaders and Civilazations are split, 
they are also asocial in any interaction they have with other leaders, because in doesn't include the player. War weariness is insanely opressive when stacked against you from multiple other civs. AI are very obnoxious and feels very dumb, truely a game where difficulty is heavily reliant on resource boosting.
The victory conditions are whack, culture is brainless, economics is boring lacking complexity, 
military is way too easy and does not even require war and lastly but not least science takes too long and also lacks complexity.

The game has an enormous identity issue, even after all the patches, it still isn't civilization, not worth the Sid Meier's title, change it to Human Kind Civilization, way more accurate. I'm gonna spare you for going through all the bug issues, ui hud interface problems, mechanics not working as intended, game crashes. The still horrible online matchmaking, which forces you to make a 2K account, on laucnh crashes, etc..

To conclude the review, the does have new creative mechanics and innovation that diffently are worth keeping and exploring more. But the towering wall of negativity is very difficult to ignore, 
especially because of the standard that they have sat an…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the user interface is difficult to read and manage, particularly regarding city visuals, tile yields, and menus.

citations.review_text:
I have had this game since launch. I have played at least one game through each of their "we are fixing it" updates. But I am done waiting and it's time to call it what it is. 

There is no point in reviewing this game independently, CIV is a series and they are supposed to improve on the previous iteration. I have a thousand hours on CIV 6, so I understand the game and the format well. 

Here is why CIV7 sucks and is potentially the CIV killer:
- There is almost zero thought process put into any other victory type save Domination. Space race is no longer a race. Cultural victory is even more confusing than CIV6 with moving goal posts and a tourism system that is not explained anywhere. And the new economic victory is somehow more boring and pointless than the religious victory. There is no way to "compete" with AI in the economic victory. There is nothing you can do to stop an isolated CIV from magically becoming an economic super power and winning. (except war of course)
 
- Visual Design and UX teams were/are still working in complete isolation. While it looks pretty when closed up, there is no way look at a city and figure out what is going on. OR tell one city from another. Even wonders don't stand out. The only way to play this game is through menus and those look ugly. So all the efforts spent on making units and buildings look beautiful is completely wasted. 

- The resource assignment is the most Kafkaesque stupidity I have seen in any game. Why is it point and click? Twice? Haven't you heard of dragging? What about resource sorting by bonus type? Is all that to hard to implement? or just too hard to think about?

- Since war is the only system they truly improved on everything AI does boils down to war. There is no diplomatic way to prevent your neighbours from declaring war on you. No matter how much influence you spend on improving relations, they will at least declare 2 wars on you per age due to the idiotic agenda system. 

- The last stra…

I've heard a lot of complaints about this game, but I found it super engrossing and fun. I like the civ switching option quite a lot. Visually, it's beautiful, once you get used to the darker aesthetic. I do wish it were a bit cleaner and easier to read in terms of tile yields and such. I think the city development mechanics are an improvement over Civ6. I imagine this game is only going to get better with continued updates.

single_points.text: One reviewer says that exceeding the city limit results in endless turns of inaction and plummets production.

citation.review_text: I've been playing every Civ game since Civ II. Civ VII is very disappointing.  I waited over a year to buy it based on reviews hoping it would get better.  Its just not fun, the city limits ruin the traditional take of the world mentality.  You have endless turns of not being able to do anything because you're city limit is over exceeded and all production plummets.  It makes the game so boring.   The ages and civilization changes just make no sense.  This is the first review I've ever left of anything because I can't stand seeing something I've loved for 3 decades be ruined by trying to copy other games that missed the mark.  I'm extremely disappointed.
